summary: Ground explicit Email Date-header claims to one complete Date value in their own citations.
decision_refs: The active objective requires accurate file-grounded questions across RFI, Submittal and Email content
An offline reproduction proved that an Email Date-header answer could borrow a Received date from the same exact citation
A bounded complete-header check closes the structured timestamp gap without timezone conversion or another model request
approval_evidence: The persistent objective authorizes bounded accuracy and adaptability improvements to the existing file-grounded question flow.
known_limitations: Only explicit Email date and Date-header claims enter this guard; generic document dates remain under the existing full-date and date-role checks.
Only evidence conservatively classified as Email can ground an Email Date header; a Received line, body date or RFI/Submittal form Date field remains a separate value.
A natural sent-date question may use the complete Date header or a separately labelled exact Sent date; no claim is made that the Date header proves transport or delivery time.
Case, repeated whitespace, outer quotation marks and answer-ending punctuation outside the value normalize while weekday, date, time, seconds, numeric offset and comments stay exact.
The guard does not decode encoded words, unfold new source formats, convert time zones, infer delivery or transport time, choose the current thread message or determine authority.
Header unfolding remains the responsibility of the existing Email parser; this change does not connect to a mailbox or alter source parsing.
